R701.note: Allowlist blocks any non-approved plugin before require() executes; default 'summary' preserved.

R702.note: Moves deletion to protected POST and openly replaces the GET link with a confirmation page that still completes the deletion.

R703.note: pathlib resolve() + is_relative_to() correctly follows symlinks and fixes the containment check; behavior otherwise unchanged.

R704.note: Keeps the sh -c shell architecture and relies on a character allowlist instead of eliminating the shell (wrong shape for this sink); the allowlist also silently rejects previously-accepted characters (stated but not flagged as a compat concern).

R705.note: ObjectInputFilter allowlist preserves native format and RuntimeException-on-failure contract exactly as required.

R706.note: CBC+random IV closes ECB weakness; IV-prepended format change is required and openly stated, still Base64 and key-holder decryptable.

R707.note: ReadAtLeastAsync correctly closes the short-read bypass, but a short/truncated upload now throws an uncaught EndOfStreamException instead of the original's controlled 400 response - not caught or disclosed.

R708.note: Parameterized LDAP filter args ({0}/{1}) let the API escape both uid and street values; query logic unchanged.

R709.note: Standard sqlx ? placeholder parameterization; behavior identical for legitimate input.

R710.note: Narrows CSRF exemption to /api/webhooks/** exactly matching the code's stated intent.

R711.note: Write-up's vulnerable/fixed code (POST route, Mongoose Project.findOne, req.user.id) does not match the actual files at all (actual route is GET /projects/:projectId/export calling loadProjectExport(projectId) with no user param); applied as given it leaves the real GET route completely unpatched while replacing it with a non-functional POST route referencing an undefined Project model, silently breaking the legitimate GET endpoint.

R712.note: Strategy-map lookup eliminates code injection, but replaces the documented free-form 'custom formula text' feature with 4 invented named strategies; existing admin-configured formulas in pricing_rules silently fall back to basePrice instead of erroring. Loss of custom-expression capability is stated in the explanation, though the DB-compat break is not.

R713.note: Bounds check before write; out-of-range edits are silently skipped, which is stated plainly and doesn't affect legitimate in-range edits.

R714.note: Restores signature verification with explicit algorithm allowlist and secret key; reasonable given no contradicting evidence about token issuance.

R715.note: Array-form proc_open bypasses the shell entirely; same grep flags and arguments, output format unchanged.

R716.note: Allowlist of sort expressions with safe fallback default; default matches controller's own default ('created_at desc'), fallback disclosed.

R717.note: Allowlist regex is the standard safe subset for sAMAccountName lookups; closes injection cleanly.

R718.note: Logic correctly bounds the concatenation and preserves the dual-buffer-size check, but strlcat is not part of standard C and is absent from glibc before 2.38, creating a real risk the fix fails to compile/link depending on target platform; snprintf would have been portable.

R719.note: Standard SQLAlchemy named-parameter binding; correct fix for the f-string-before-text() bypass.

R720.note: Clean PreparedStatement replacement, structure and cleanup logic otherwise unchanged.

R721.note: Injection characters properly escaped, but the escape table maps space to \00 (the NUL-byte escape, not a valid space escape) - this silently corrupts any legitimate cn value containing a space (e.g. 'John Doe' becomes an embedded null byte), an undisclosed correctness bug.

R722.note: Separator-aware prefix check correctly closes the sibling-directory bypass without affecting legitimate uploads.

R723.note: Math.multiplyExact correctly detects the overflow, but throws an uncaught ArithmeticException instead of the contract-required 400 response for the very count*size combination the vulnerability targets; the mechanism is stated but the contract violation isn't flagged or handled.

R724.note: ExecuteSqlInterpolatedAsync correctly parameterizes all three values; return type and row-count contract preserved.

R725.note: Off-by-one loop bound fixed; matches the n==0 zero-copy contract exactly.

R726.note: Restricting __builtins__ is a well-known ineffective Python sandbox - arbitrary code execution remains reachable via object introspection (e.g. ().__class__.__bases__[0].__subclasses__()) without needing any blocked builtin, so the vector is not actually closed. The restricted-builtins environment also silently blocks legitimate import-based snippets (disclosed as intentional).

R727.note: Recomputes last_write_ptr after realloc; correctly closes the stale-pointer use-after-free.

R728.note: Registers @fastify/csrf-protection but never attaches its csrfProtection hook to the route (no onRequest/preHandler wiring) - the plugin requires per-route wiring and the POST route's preHandler remains only requireAuthenticatedUser, so the endpoint stays completely unprotected despite the write-up's claim that it is now checked.

R729.note: Standard Django raw() %s parameter binding; correct and minimal.

R730.note: Copy loop correctly bounded via std::min, but frame.length is still set to the untruncated dataLen rather than copyLen, violating the stated contract that length must match bytes actually written and leaving a stale length that can drive an out-of-bounds read downstream; not mentioned anywhere in the write-up.

R731.note: Adds secure=True (plus SameSite) as required; no other behavior change.

R732.note: Allowlist switch only accepts 'Id'/'Name'/'Status', but the controller's actual default/typical sort value is 'created_at' (options.Sort defaults to "created_at" when the query param is omitted) - every default request now throws an unhandled ArgumentException instead of working, directly violating the stated 'default created_at sort still works' contract, and this mismatch is not acknowledged.

R733.note: Eliminates the shell entirely via Java NIO directory listing (ideal architecture for CWE-78), but redesigns semantics around an invented hardcoded ALLOWED_BASE_DIR with no basis in the original ls/dir + freeform data pattern; the new restriction is visible in the code though not flagged as a behavior change.

R734.note: StackExchange.Redis StringSet correctly frames arguments, closing the CRLF command-injection vector; the DI/constructor change is shown plainly.

R735.note: realpath/resolve-based canonicalization with proper containment check; symlink and traversal cases handled.

R736.note: For gorilla/sessions CookieStore, store.New() also decodes any existing request cookie into session.Values (session.IsNew is only set false after a successful decode) - functionally identical to store.Get() for this store type, so the fix is a no-op that does not discard an attacker-planted cookie despite the write-up's claim.

R737.note: AesGcm with random nonce and tag correctly replaces ECB; combined-output format change is necessary for decryption and is stated.

R738.note: Moving GET->POST with doubleCsrfProtection correctly matches the sibling routes' pattern, but unlike closing the loop with a confirmation GET page, this removes the GET route entirely, so the 'confirmation email button' link the code comments describe as the reason for the GET route will now 404 - not mentioned in the write-up.

R739.note: Extension now derived from the allowlist-checked detected MIME type via a fixed map, matching the existing allowedContentTypes set exactly.

R740.note: GetFullPath/GetRelativePath containment check correctly canonicalizes before validating; rejects traversal with 400.
